authoredNote: Transcribed from a measured run (script/m14/tmp/dt-fixture-dump.ts) against this file. The DECLARING half of the two-file local-read fixture; see `reads.expectation.json` for the property the pair exists for. Its content is deliberately the most ordinary shape available — one class, one int field, a common English name — because the defect the pair pins needs no unusual input: it needs only that some declaration in the project happens to carry the local's name exactly once.
rationale: Exists so the collision is REAL. The reading file's local is named `counter`; this file declares a `counter` field on an unrelated class in an unrelated file. Under the bare-name rule that was the entire requirement for the store to bind a function's own local to this field — one declaration of that name in the project, in any file, meaning anything. The pair is what makes `reads.expectation.json`'s forbid row a statement about a measurable collision instead of a hypothetical one, and it is why the two files live in one sub-directory (the harness treats a sub-directory as one project). The pins here are the ordinary ones a class fixture carries; the interesting row is in the sibling.

expectRelationships.comment: the field's own name line — the declaration the bare spelling of the sibling's local read would have bound to
